problem_solving_image: The product is the unchanged central hero, with perfectly preserved geometry, materials, proportions, and branding, exactly as shown in the provided reference image. Create a single cohesive, premium lifestyle-studio image (not split-screen, not before/after) that communicates problem-solving as “something was missing, now it’s complete” through composition and context. Set the product prominently in the foreground on a clean craft desk surface (pressed cotton paper or pale natural wood) with warm natural window light and soft shadows; keep the product tack-sharp and branding fully visible. In the midground, show a work-in-progress with a clearly defined area that looks void/empty—an intentional blank space, unfinished section, or missing element (e.g., an unfilled shape outline, a reserved blank panel on a card, an empty border area, a lightly penciled guide with nothing applied yet). Right next to that void area, show the solution happening: the product actively being used to complete it in a believable way (clean coverage filling the blank, crisp linework completing the outline, a neatly applied layer finishing the reserved area, or a precise alignment completing the composition). The “empty” portion must read as intentional and lacking, while the completed portion reads as satisfying, clean, and controlled—no messy chaos, no exaggerated transformation effects. Keep the workspace realistically lived-in but tidy: a few craft tools at the far edges only, softly out of focus, with the area around the product kept clear. Composition: product in the foreground as the strongest element, the empty/unfinished area visible nearby, and the newly completed result clearly visible on the same sheet/canvas. Background: soft warm-to-neutral gradient or simple studio falloff, bright and optimistic. No text, no dramatic filters, no side-by-side framing.
